model_interpretation.claim: Fusing absolute value into the grid-stride reduction avoids the scratch write/read and one kernel launch. A grid of ceil(n/256), capped at 1024 CTAs, avoids needless atomics for small inputs while bounding CTA-level atomics for large inputs. Whether those savings offset the required output reset and atomic contention must be measured; the controller must validate FP64 tolerance for every required size and seed.

model_interpretation.claim: Reducing the large-input grid cap from 1024 to 256 limits output atomics to at most 256 per call while preserving one input pass and the per-call reset. This may reduce contention, but it may also reduce memory-level parallelism; the controller should compare total time including reset and launch overhead and validate every required size and the FP64 tolerance.

model_interpretation.applicability: The current parent using a 1024-CTA cap was correct on all 10 reported cases and measured 0.4474 ms mean; that result does not isolate the cap's effect or establish that fewer CTAs will be faster.
model_interpretation.next_experiment: Measure this 256-CTA cap under the same protocol, including output reset and launch overhead, and compare correctness and timing with the parent.

items.subject: Single-kernel CTA aggregation with output atomics
items.objective: Evaluate a distinct single-kernel alternative: reset output in the default stream, stream input once, reduce locally per CTA, then atomicAdd one CTA result to output. Explore keeping CTA atomic count modest; do not rely on scratch initialization or omit the per-call reset. Compare total time including reset and launch overhead against hierarchical candidates, and validate every required size and the FP64 tolerance.
